decisions.question: S13 declared publish<T extends Object?, V extends T>(MultiWriterTopic<T>, V) instead of the publish<T, V extends T> the orchestrator named, because the named form makes a failed inference fall back to dynamic, which adds inference_failure_on_function_invocation under strict-inference and breaks navigation-api@v1's reject/current_route_is_claimed_by_the_executor.dart (experiment T10). Is the written-out bound a different change from the one authorized, making this a run-stop?

options.label: Same change; accept
options.consequence: The amendment stands: wrong value types do not compile, a state topic still reports argument_type_not_assignable alone, and no fixture outside bus-api@v1 changes.

options.label: Different change; treat the named form as a breaking amendment and stop
options.consequence: The owner decides between two spellings of one signature, one of which breaks a consumer fixture and one of which does not.

decisions.why: The authorization was for the change's effect: restore Spec §4.2's compile-time type check on publish without breaking any other contract's fixtures. The written-out bound has the same subtyping relation and is the only spelling that meets the second condition; experiment T10 shows the named spelling would have broken navigation-api@v1. The breaking-amend stop guards existing consumers, and the accepted form breaks none.
